executiveSummary: Surveillance data spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to generate Elevated concern in the Americas with ongoing animal-human interface risks flagged in both November 2025 and March 2026 updates. Mpox transmission persists in the Americas region as of April 2026, while Yellow Fever activity prompted a formal epidemiological alert in March 2026. Additional pressure comes from simultaneous circulation of dengue, chikungunya, measles, pertussis, and respiratory pathogens across multiple regions, indicating a high-burden multi-pathogen environment.
bottomLine: The Americas and Europe face a complex, multi-threat epidemiological landscape dominated by Avian Influenza A(H5N1) zoonotic spillover risk, Mpox resurgence, Yellow Fever, and surging vector-borne and vaccine-preventable diseases requiring coordinated surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Dual PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained animal-sector activity
Ongoing zoonotic spillover risk at human-animal interface in the Americas
Animal category classification with human spillover potential requiring heightened surveillance
threats.action: Enhance surveillance at human-animal interfaces, strengthen farm biosecurity, expand testing of exposed individuals, and maintain antiviral stockpile readiness

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 indicating active transmission
Ongoing circulation in the Americas requiring sustained public health response
Cross-regional spread risk given international travel corridors
threats.action: Accelerate vaccination campaigns in high-risk populations, enhance case detection and contact tracing, coordinate with ECDC on cross-regional transmission monitoring

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: Formal PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026
Active circulation triggering alert-level response in endemic and bordering areas
Risk of spread to unvaccinated urban populations
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in affected and at-risk areas, strengthen vector control, issue travel advisories, and ensure vaccine supply chain integrity

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 18 2026 indicating significant regional activity
High case burden historically associated with early-year peaks in the Americas
Simultaneous circulation with chikungunya amplifying Aedes aegypti-driven transmission pressure
threats.action: Intensify vector control programs, strengthen hospital surge capacity, promote community source reduction, and enhance arboviral integrated surveillance

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Syncytial Virus
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses and Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert January 2026 flagging simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation
PAHO April 2026 alert marking start of Southern Hemisphere 2026 season
ECDC weekly communicable disease threat reports weeks 16-20 covering influenza activity in Europe
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination for eligible populations, monitor ICU capacity, ensure antiviral availability, and track strain evolution for vaccine mismatch signals

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained elevated incidence
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning immunity and vaccine coverage gaps
Infant mortality risk in under-vaccinated populations
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage by age cohort, accelerate catch-up immunization, reinforce maternal Tdap vaccination, and strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026
Resurgence risk linked to pandemic-era immunization disruptions
High transmission potential in susceptible communities
threats.action: Conduct supplementary immunization activities in areas with coverage below 95%, strengthen case-based surveillance, and ensure rapid response team readiness

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
threats.pathogen: Hantavirus (Sin Nombre and Andes virus strains)
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 19 2025
High case fatality rate associated with pulmonary syndrome presentations
Seasonal rodent population dynamics increasing exposure risk in rural communities
threats.action: Enhance rodent control programs, strengthen clinical awareness and early case recognition, ensure diagnostic laboratory access, and issue public communication on exposure prevention

selectAgentSummary: No explicit BSL-3 or BSL-4 select agent laboratory detections were reported in the available surveillance report titles and metadata. However, Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is a BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential and is flagged as Elevated threat based on dual PAHO updates across the Americas. Yellow Fever virus, also BSL-3, triggered a formal PAHO alert in March 2026. Hantavirus, a BSL-3 agent with high case fatality rate, prompted a December 2025 PAHO alert. All three warrant heightened biosafety protocols and coordinated public health response.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific signals identified in available report titles; Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance surveillance recommended given resurgence patterns; influenza antiviral resistance monitoring warranted given dual-season circulation pressure
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen co-circulation in the Americas creating compounded healthcare system burden across 2025-2026
Vaccine-preventable disease resurgence (measles, pertussis) consistent with pandemic-era immunization gap recovery phase
Dual PAHO H5N1 updates within four months suggest sustained and potentially expanding zoonotic transmission interface in the Americas
Seasonal influenza Southern Hemisphere 2026 season onset coinciding with Northern Hemisphere late-season activity creating extended global transmission window
Vector-borne disease co-circulation of dengue and chikungunya amplifying Aedes-driven transmission pressure with potential for diagnostic misclassification
Non-infectious public health threats emerging alongside biological threats, including GLP-1 medication misuse and methanol poisoning alerts in the Americas
